The Destination

Nosy Sakatia

Just a short boat transfer from Nosy Be, the tranquil island of Nosy Sakatia offers a peaceful and authentic alternative to its livelier neighbour. Often referred to as the “Island of Orchids” due to the many wild orchids found there, it is also nicknamed the “Island of Turtles” because of the green turtles that feed on the sea grass beds in the surrounding waters. Nosy Sakatia is known for its unspoilt beaches, traditional villages and rich marine life, making it a hidden gem for travellers seeking a slower, more immersive island experience.

With no large-scale development and a strong sense of community, Nosy Sakatia captures the essence of Madagascar’s coastal charm — where time slows down and nature takes centre stage.

Natural Beauty

Nature & Wildlife

Nosy Sakatia is fringed by quiet beaches, rocky coves and vibrant coral reefs. Its calm, shallow waters are ideal for snorkelling and are home to an abundance of marine life. The island is particularly famous for its resident population of green sea turtles, which can often be seen grazing on seagrass beds just offshore — an unforgettable experience for visitors.

Inland, the island features small plantations of vanilla, orchids and tropical fruits, alongside traditional Malagasy homes and fishing communities. The combination of natural beauty and cultural authenticity makes Nosy Sakatia a uniquely enriching destination.

Experiences

Things to Do in Nosy Sakatia

Snorkelling with Sea Turtles

One of the island’s most iconic experiences is swimming alongside green sea turtles in their natural habitat. The calm conditions make this accessible for all levels of swimmers.

Diving & Marine Exploration

Explore coral reefs teeming with tropical fish, octopus and other marine species. The surrounding waters are relatively untouched, offering excellent visibility and biodiversity.

Kayaking & Paddleboarding

The island’s sheltered waters are perfect for gentle ocean activities, allowing guests to explore the coastline at their own pace.

Island Walks & Village Visits

Take guided walks through local villages and plantations to gain insight into daily life on the island. Learn about traditional farming, fishing practices and Malagasy culture.

Fishing & Boat Excursions

Join local fishermen or set out on private boat trips to discover nearby islands, secluded beaches and hidden snorkelling spots.

Sunset Cruises

End the day with a relaxed cruise along the coastline, taking in the spectacular colours of the Indian Ocean at sunset.

Where to Stay

Accommodation in Nosy Sakatia

Accommodation on Nosy Sakatia is intimate, laid-back and designed to blend seamlessly with the island’s natural surroundings. With a focus on privacy and personalised service, properties here offer a home-away-from-home atmosphere combined with authentic island living.

Private beachfront villas and bungalows set within tropical gardens
Spacious living areas ideal for families, couples or small groups
Fully serviced stays with attentive staff and locally inspired cuisine
Flexible experiences including access to private boats and tailored excursions
A strong connection to the surrounding environment and local community
Some properties are particularly well suited to travellers looking for exclusivity and flexibility, offering both accommodation and private charter options to explore the surrounding archipelago.

As part of a bespoke itinerary with The Madagascar Collection, Nosy Sakatia pairs beautifully with nearby islands and mainland destinations, creating a well-rounded journey through one of the Indian Ocean’s most captivating regions.

Highlights

  • Resident green sea turtle population year-round
  • Snorkelling in calm, crystal-clear waters
  • Wild orchids & vanilla plantations
  • Kayaking & paddleboarding in sheltered bays
  • Traditional Malagasy fishing village visits
  • Private boat charters to nearby islands
  • Sunset cruises along the coastline
  • Short transfer from Nosy Be

When to Visit

Year-Round
The turtles are resident year-round, making Nosy Sakatia a rewarding visit in any month.
May – October
Dry season. Calmest waters and best snorkelling visibility.
July – September
Humpback whales passing through the surrounding channel.

Combine With

  • Nosy Be — island base & excursions
  • Nosy Komba — lemur forest walks
  • Nosy Iranja — the iconic sandbar
  • Nosy Ankazoberavina — private island escape
